chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman who sees in sleep that a man is copulating with her in her private part, until she discharges. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should wash.' And in another report, he said: 'Upon her is a washing, but do not narrate this to them, lest they take it as an excuse.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who discharges semen during sleep?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the parity between men and women regarding the obligation of ghusl upon seminal discharge during sleep, a ruling derived from the general principle of major ritual impurity. Shaykh al-Kulayni includes the caution against publicizing this ruling to prevent 'excuse-makers' (mutakhallifin) from treating nocturnal emission as a license for frequent sexual activity, reflecting the Shia scholarly concern with balancing legal ease with spiritual discipline.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the woman who sees during the sleep that the man is copulating with her in her private part, until she discharges. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She should wash’.
And in another report, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon her is a washing, but she should not narrate with this (to others), so she would be seized by trouble’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a woman who in her dream finds a man who engages in an intercourse with her until she experiences orgasm. He (the Imam) said, ‘She must take Ghusl (bath).”’ According to another Hadith, she must take Ghusl (bath) but must not inform others to avoid ridicule.
